CC|The 41kD, 37kD and 36kD forms of <fbsym>FBgn0002855==Acp26Aa</fbsym> protein differ in the extent of
| glycosylation. The 36kD species is far less abundant than the other two. By
| tracking with region-specific antibodies, it was shown that the 41kD
| species is processed to 38kD, 33kD and finally to 28kD while the 37kD
| species is processed to 33kD, 30kD and finally 25kD in parallel processing
| pathways. These processing steps were shown to consist of stepwise cleavage
| events in the N-terminal half of the protein. The processing sites were
| mapped by CNBr mapping and by analysis of conservated cle vage sites within
| several Drosophila species. Finally, it was found that accessory gland main
| cell secretions are necessary to process <fbsym>FBgn0002855==Acp26Aa</fbsym> protein in the female
| genital tract.

BODP|In the pre-blastoderm embryo (stage 2) <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> protein is localized
| basal to the plasma membrane.  At the syncitial blastoderm stage (stage 3)
| <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> is then concentrated around the nuclei which have migrated
| close tothe plasma membrane and this concentration is termed "spectrin
| caps".  Prior to cellularization (stage 3 to 4), these "spectrin caps"
| elongate and become narrowed where the daughter caps (and daughter nuclei)
| will separate.  As the mitotic divisions cease, the concentration of
| <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> around the nuclei decreases and shows a more uniform
| distribution near the plasma membrane.  During cellularization (satge 5)
| <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> marks the position of cleavage furrow formation and persists
| along the cleavage furrow. Cytoplasmic expression of <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> is noted
| along the lateral sides of the forming cell membrane.  After the completion
| of cellularization, <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> is localized more uniformly at the plasma
| membrane.  During gastrulation (stage 6), <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> protein
| concentrations remain high, with highest levels detected in the
| amnioproctodeal invagination and the cephalic furrow near the apical region
| of these cells.  During germ band extention, <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> protein is
| distributed in all cells, with particularly high concentrations in the
| spiracles and tracheal pits.  The overall <fbsym>&agr;-Spec</fbsym> protein
| concentration increases over the course of embryogenesis, with the highest
| levels present at the end of embryonic development.

CC|Site directed mutagenesis was used to create 4 mutants. In each, a conserved
| glutamic acid residue within one of the Ca[2+]-binding sites has been
| replaced with glutamine, thus creating four CAL proteins with analagous
| mutations in each of the Ca[2+]-binding sites. Conformational studies on
| these mutants confirm that the carboxy-terminal two sites show cooperative
| Ca[2+] binding which produces a major change in the protein conformation.
| The amino terminal Ca[2+]-binding sites show more independent properties
| with respect to Ca[2+] binding and conformational change. Mutants at the
| amino-terminal sites were shown to affect conformational change induced by
| Ca[2+] binding at the carboxy-terminal end. This work supports the idea
| that the carboxy-terminal sites are high affinity for Ca[2+] binding and
| the amino-terminal sites are lower affinity.
